title: Release guardrails & pinboard (personal scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
This is my personal scratchpad for the upcoming release window (v2025.02.1). Focus is on canary guardrails, version pinning heuristics and the observability checklist I want to run during the first 6 hours. Rapid notes to self + commands + quick queries. Not polished; will extract checklist for official runbook later.

High-level goal:
- Push model-serving runtime and routing change with minimal user-visible regressions.
- Keep steady-state latency and error-rate within SLOs and catch quality regressions early using small cohorts and automated checks.

Quick summary (decision ladder):
- Start canary at 0.5% traffic to control clients (internal + beta partners) for 20m warmup.
- If no regressions, ramp to 2% for 40m.
- If still clean, 10% for 1h across more cohorts.
- If all green at 10% and cost/latency acceptable, schedule 50% split for 2h then full rollover overnight.

Primary owners (on-call during release window):
- Release lead: Nora Patel (me) – coordinate traffic, roll/pin decisions
- Runtime lead: Ethan Liu – kernel selection / instance sizing
- Observability: Maya Rodriguez – dashboards, anomaly triage
- Escalation: SRE pager (team: eng-sre)

Pinning / version policy notes:
- Default behavior: tenant-facing pin at route-level (route config) – do not apply org-wide pin without explicit approval.
- If a tenant sees >3x token-cost variance or >1.5x tail latency, pin back to previous model variant for that tenant only.
- For dedicated customers, contact account owner before automatic pinning. Add a ticket and notify CS.
- CLI to pin quickly (notes to self):
  - rwctl rollout pin --tenant <TENANT_ID> --route <ROUTE> --model v2025.01.7 --reason "auto-rollback/canary"
  - rwctl rollout revert --route <ROUTE> --to-traffic-snapshot <SNAPSHOT_ID>

Canary cohorts (practical mapping):
- Internal devices: API key set_internal_canary_01 (0.2%): team dev + perf tests
- Beta customers: key_beta_cohort (0.3%): handpicked customers who agreed to test
- Public cohort: seeded hashes for 0.5% after internal green
- Edge cases: dedicated tenants excluded unless we explicitly enable in the canary config

Traffic schedule (conservative):
- T0: 0m -> 0.5% (internal only) – 20m
- T1: 20m -> 2% (internal + beta) – 40m
- T2: 60m -> 10% (public seeded) – 60m
- T3: 120m -> 50% (if green) – 120m
- T4: 240m -> full (overnight finalization)

Automatic abort criteria (fail-fast):
- Request-level error rate increase: additional 0.2% absolute or 50% relative over baseline for 5m
- Latency p95 increase by >50ms over baseline for 10m
- Token-generation throughput drop >25% (unexpected capacity issues)
- Quality alarms from eval set: BLEU/ROUGE style metric regression >3% on smoke prompt set
- Cost shock: per-token cost increase >30% for 10m

Manual abort triggers (require release lead sign-off):
- One or more high-severity customer-reported incidents for production non-dedicated tenants
- Unexpected model hallucination patterns flagged by QA channel

Telemetry & quick queries (notes/examples):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 per route (BigQuery):
  SELECT route, quantiles(latency_ms, 0.5, 0.95, 0.99) FROM tokens_stream WHERE ts >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 15 MINUTE) GROUP BY route;
- Error rate by stage (proxy/runtime/model) – watch 502/504/5xx counts.
- Token cost delta by model: compare token_cost(model=v2025.02.1) vs token_cost(model=v2025.01.7) over last 30m.
- Quality smoke set (eval harness): run 50 prompts from /eval/smoke-canary-50 and diff aggregate. Automation note: ensure harness runs within first 10m of each ramp.

Dashboards / alerts to open at T0:
- Routing health dashboard: p50/p95/p999, errors, request volume split (canary vs control)
- KV cache hit-rate trend (to catch cache invalidation regressions)
- GPU utilisation per pool (watch for uneven packing after kernel changes)
- Cost per token trending for top 5 customers

Immediate quick commands (keep on clipboard):
- curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/<ROUTE>/traffic" – inspect current traffic split
- rwctl rollout status --route <ROUTE> --follow
- kubectl logs -n runtime $(kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=runtime --field-selector=status.phase=Running | head -n1) -c runner | tail -n 200

Safety mitigations I want in place before T1:
- One-click revert button wired to previous traffic snapshot (confirm snapshot ID and TTL)
- Canary silently disabled for dedicated customers
- Auto-pin policy enabled for error spikes (with notification)
- Rolling restart window: stagger restarts across AZs to avoid correlated cold starts

Post-ramp checklist (first 6 hours):
- 0–1h after 100%: watch top-10 customers latency, spike detection on p95, token-cost variance
- 1–3h: check SAMPLER logs for drift in generation distribution (token entropy shifts)
- 3–6h: run extended eval (200 prompts) and compare to baseline. If any regression flagged, start rollback process.
- Create post-release ticket with snapshots, graphs, and decisions (label REL-893-postmortem)

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-up):
- Confirm whether per-tenant pinning writes are audit-logged in our central audit stream (ask security).
- Add an automated smoke eval that runs in staging parity and gets triggered as part of canary ramp (Maya owns).
- Should we include a short-circuit for cost (reduce batch-size to limit spend) or better to simply halt ramp? (pros/cons)
- Review canary cohort list to ensure no high-value customers are accidentally included (sync with CS).

Notes to self (less formal):
- Keep the early ramps during US morning to maximize overlap with eng & SRE. Avoid Friday releases unless unavoidable.
- If I see small latency blips but no errors, hold ramp for extra 30m and re-run smoke eval.
- Remember to update route change comment with exact PR link and snapshot id so we can trace later.

Retrospective prompts (what to capture if we finish):
- Was the ramp schedule too conservative / aggressive?
- Did automatic abort thresholds trigger appropriately? Too sensitive?
- Any gaps in telemetry visibility or dashboarding?
- Were communications to CS and customers timely and clear?

End-of-note: extract two actionable items for the formal runbook:
1) Add explicit per-tenant pin policy with audit logging + CS notification flow.
2) Implement a canary-smoke-eval automation that blocks ramp for 10m until it passes.

-- Nora (scratchpad)
